listitem.simpara: Started guidance for defining change control narratives.

chapter.simpara: Narratives express proposed and completed project changes through a user story and its supporting backstory. Start them from documentation/templates/narrative.xml and retain only the lifecycle activities that apply.

section.title: How true is the backstory?
section.simpara: Every narrative opens with a backstory, and every backstory says how much of it really happened. The answer goes in the required backstory attribute of the narrative's root element, and it tells readers how far the story proves that the issue exists, and how far it only illustrates the value of resolving it.

listitem.simpara: The backstory is, in substance, an account of something that really happened. Changing names or smoothing details to protect people does not make it any less true.

The backstory is anchored in something real — an actual event, a real person's situation, a remark someone really made — and completed with invented elements. A persona assembled from several real cases belongs here.
The backstory is invented to illustrate the value of resolving the issue. It may be perfectly realistic, even informed by years of experience, but no specific real case lies behind it.

section.simpara: When in doubt, ask yourself: can I point to a real observation behind this story? If not, it is fiction, because general experience does not count and a specific case does. If you can, but you invented parts of it, it is mixed. If you invented almost nothing, it is a true story.
